title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues item f) of a list of research directions. The previous page treated motivic representations of Γ_Q built from representations of SL(2,Z)'. Here Grothendieck names a second direction that he finds very attractive. It does not need group schemes and can be pursued with the profinite ('gros') fundamental groups alone.

(1) Study certain particular Q-rational points of M_{0,3,Q} = P^1_Q − {0,1,∞}. Each such point x gives a splitting (a section, up to conjugacy) of the arithmetic fundamental group extension 1 → π̂_{0,3} → M_{0,3} → Γ_Q → 1, written M^+_{0,3} ≃ π_1(M_{0,3,Q}, S_3) on the previous page.

(2) Extract from these sections further 'arithmetic' properties of π̂_{0,3} and of the outer Galois action on it, of the type Ihara obtained ([Iha] is presumably Ihara's work on Galois representations on the pro-ℓ/profinite π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞}, the Fermat/Jacobi-sum results).

(3) Do semi-explicit computations of the extension M_{0,3} (equivalently, of the Galois action on path torsors) at points other than the 'critical' ones. The critical points are 0, 1, ∞ and the points with nontrivial stabilizer under the S_3 action on P^1 − {0,1,∞}. One orbit is 1/2, 2, −1, each fixed by an involution: z ↦ 1−z, z ↦ z/(z−1), z ↦ 1/z respectively. The other is −j, −j̄, the primitive 6th roots of unity, fixed by the 3-cycles z ↦ 1/(1−z), z ↦ 1−1/z. Splittings at these critical points are what the notes use. The next page composes with the maps Π̂_{0,3} → M̂_{0,3} attached to 1/2 and −j, matching them with the splittings ψ_ρ, ψ_σ at the group-scheme level. The remark 'moralement des pointés, pour le moment!' shows that base points at 0, 1, ∞ are not yet rigorously defined.

(4) The parenthesis flags the foundational issue. It must be secured by 'la méthode suggérée par Deligne': study the loop equation ('équation des lacets') in a partial compactification, i.e. what became tangential base points at the boundary. One must also check invariance or compatibility of the fundamental groups involved, in particular the role of the complex points (here underlined).

In modern terms, (1)–(3) form the programme of Galois actions on étale path torsors from a (tangential) base point to arbitrary rational points z ∈ P^1(Q)−{0,1,∞}. This is the ℓ-adic/profinite analogue of evaluating polylogarithms and associators at z. It is also tied to the sections of π_1 coming from rational points, the subject of the section conjecture.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The list of critical points is correct: 1/2, 2, −1 are the fixed points of the three involutions of S_3, and −j, −j̄ (roots of z^2−z+1) are the fixed points of the 3-cycles. Note that −j, −j̄ are not Q-rational individually; only their pair (orbit) is defined over Q. So 'points rationnels' applies to them only in a Galois-orbit sense.
Gap acknowledged by the author: the base points 0, 1, ∞ are used only 'morally' (see next page). Rigour requires Deligne's tangential base points, which the parenthesis explicitly defers.

ideas.what: Use sections of the arithmetic π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞} attached to particular Q-rational points to obtain arithmetic information on the profinite π_1 and the Galois action
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on étale path torsors / sections at rational points; ℓ-adic polylogarithms at z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1980s), Deligne (1989), Wojtkowiak (ℓ-adic polylogarithms, 1990s–2000s), Nakamura and Wojtkowiak (explicit formulae)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions the Galois action on π̂_1 and the role of rational/tangential points; section conjecture letter to Faltings (1983) for sections from rational points

ideas.what: The S_3-'critical' points 1/2, 2, −1, −j, −j̄ as special base points giving canonical splittings
ideas.modern_name: Fixed points of the anharmonic group action; base points used e.g. in Ihara/Drinfeld-type relations and in GT-related computations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (anharmonic group); used in Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature (Drinfeld 1990, Ihara)

ideas.what: Foundations via Deligne's suggestion: treat base points at the boundary via a partial compactification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points')
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (tangential base points discussed in relation to the Teichmüller tower)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes semi-explicit computation of the extension/Galois action at non-critical rational points of P^1−{0,1,∞}. He frames it as compatible with his loop-equation ('équation des lacets') approach. The idea was later realized by others (Wojtkowiak, Nakamura, Anderson–Ihara), so it is an anticipation rather than a gap in the literature.
missed.quote: des calculs semi-explicites de l'extension M_{0,3} ... en d'autres points que les points "critiques" 0, 1, ∞, 1/2, 2, −1, −j, −j̄
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, it documents that Grothendieck envisaged path-torsor computations at general rational points, independently of and possibly before the ℓ-adic polylogarithm literature. Mathematically it adds nothing new.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a programmatic outline of a direction later developed extensively (Galois action on path torsors to rational points, tangential base points via Deligne). It contains no finished result, and the ideas are broadly consistent with Esquisse and later literature. It is of mild historical interest for the explicit attribution of the tangential-base-point method to Deligne and the explicit list of S_3-critical points.
